title: The Airy edge of shear hydrodynamics: a large-d law for the critical point of the AdS_{d+1} black brane, with a numerical radius bound at d = 512, 1024 and 8192
description:
In plain words. Holography is a way of modelling a hot plasma with a black hole in one extra dimension. Stirred gently, such a plasma flows like a fluid, and physicists write that fluid behaviour as a series. The series only works up to a certain point. In 2019 Grozdanov, Kovtun, Starinets and Tadić showed what sets it: a collision between the slow fluid ripple and one of the plasma's faster-decaying ripples. We followed that collision point from 3 up to 32768 dimensions. It creeps towards a fixed spot at a rate of one over the cube root of the dimension, with a coefficient given by Airy functions. The formula was derived without fitting, by a method that gives no error bounds. The headline forward test was not a blind test in the strict sense, as the record states. Failures are listed as failures.

The idea in one picture. you can trust a road map only up to the nearest pothole, even if the pothole sits off to the side of the road you drive on. Here the 'side' is mathematical: the trouble spot sits at a complex wavenumber, not on any real road. Where the picture breaks. a map has no single centre, while this series is built around zero wavenumber, so the limit is a circle of trust around zero.

For specialists. The critical point that limits shear hydrodynamics of the AdS_{d+1} black brane approaches (qfr^2, wfr) = (-2, i) as d^-1/3, with a coefficient fixed by the first zero of Ai'^2 - U Ai^2, derived by formal matched asymptotics (no error bounds); (qfr^2 + 2) - 2i(wfr - i) = 4/d + O(d^-4/3). A parameter-free matched model predicted the point at d = 8192-32768 to 8e-6 down to 8e-7 in qfr^2, with its form shaped on d <= 4096 and the blind values already on disk; the leading law alone misses by 1.36e-3 at d = 8192. A numerical monodromy census places the radius of convergence of the shear hydro series in [|c0| - dr, |c0|] at d = 512, 1024 and 8192, barring a pole or a cancelling branch-point pair within one sector; a coefficient route is consistent at d = 2048 only. Every scored prediction was written and hashed before its target was read, except where flagged; failures are reported as failures. Contains the preprint, data, code that regenerates the headline numbers, and the sealed-test records. Companion to doi:10.5281/zenodo.23940227.

Links. Repository, with a plain-language guide: github.com/Hashirama1337s/airy-edge-hydrodynamics. All projects: the Moki & Julio lab map.

Prepared with AI assistance; what was checked, and by what, is stated above.
